articles.title: Major fuel price rollbacks set Nov. 10 with gasoline seen to fall P16.8
articles.summary: Motorists face sharply lower pump prices Tuesday.

blocks.text: November 9, 2026 | 10:00am
Passenger buses are seen on a road with other motorists in Manila on Sept. 22, 2026.
AFP / Ted Aljibe
MANILA, Philippines — Motorists can finally expected sharply lower pump prices Tuesday, led by a P16.80-per-liter cut in gasoline after several weeks of mixed adjustments.
The Department of Energy announced the following changes Monday, November 9:

items: Gasoline: down P16.80 per liter
Diesel: down P4.10 per liter
Kerosene: down P3.70 per liter

blocks.text: The new prices are expected to remain in effect through Monday, November 16.
The rollback follows last week's P3.50-per-liter increase in gasoline. Diesel and kerosene prices fell by P1 and P1.90 per liter, respectively.
Industry forecasts late last week had pointed to smaller cuts, particularly for gasoline. The DOE has yet to clarify whether the reductions will be implemented in full Tuesday or staggered.
Global oil prices have come under pressure as concerns eased over further U.S. strikes on Iran following Democratic gains in the midterm elections.
The party's gains in both chambers of Congress strengthened its ability to oppose legislative measures supporting further U.S. military action in the Middle East.

U.S. President Donald Trump also told CNN that future attacks on Iran were "unlikely" if negotiations progressed over Tehran's nuclear program and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments.
The peso, meanwhile, remained near the P63-to-$1 level, opening at P63.06 against the dollar Monday.
Because petroleum products are traded in dollars, a stronger peso lowers the local-currency cost of imported fuel, while a weaker peso makes those purchases more expensive.

articles.title: The ocean can be our best bet vs climate change. It’s finally at the heart of COP31.
articles.summary: A healthy ocean — which is finally getting its moment at this year's United Nations climate talks — is considered 'nature's greatest climate regulator' and an integral key to reducing emissions.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – World leaders, lobbyists, and advocates are coming together in Antalya, Turkey, for the annual United Nations (UN) Climate Change Conference (COP31), which is being pegged as the “Blue COP” for its focus on the ocean.

Turkey is leading this year’s climate negotiations with Australia, pushing forward the concerns of Pacific Island countries vulnerable to rising seas, ocean warming, and acidification. Ocean action is also among Turkey’s top priorities, with the goal of “enhancing the climate resilience of coastal and marine ecosystems.”
Australian Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen, the president of negotiations at COP31, called the ocean “nature’s greatest climate regulator.”
“COP31 is an opportunity to show what cooperation can deliver at this crucial time for both our climate and global energy security,” Bowen said in a statement Thursday, November 5.
“It will be about unlocking finance and investment, cheaper energy for households, accelerating electrification, and boosting action on the ocean, nature’s greatest climate regulator.”

The UN, meanwhile, called the ocean “the world’s greatest ally against climate change,” a great stabilizer of the Earth’s climate, but one that is suffering damage because of hotter global temperatures.

This year’s COP will also focus heavily on electrification — a response to the fuel supply shock and global energy crisis that upended economies. UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell took note that the summit “takes place against the backdrop of an ongoing fossil fuel cost crisis, which has sent energy and transport costs spiraling.”

The ocean covers more than 70% of the world. It works as a buffer against the worst impacts of climate change by absorbing carbon dioxide emissions and heat from the atmosphere. Yet it has been historically absent in the climate negotiations.
Only in recent years has there been a growing momentum to actively integrate the ocean into climate talks.
Ocean-based actions can close the emissions gap — or help countries close the gap between their declared climate targets and the amount of emissions they are actually reducing — by up to 35%.

These “ocean-based actions” can take various forms: restoring marine ecosystems such as mangroves and seagrass beds, phasing out offshore oil and gas production, or cutting down emissions of maritime industries like shipping, coastal tourism, and aquatic food production.

Marine Lecerf, head of international policy at Ocean & Climate Platform, noted that the ocean was only first explicitly mentioned in the preamble of the Paris Agreement in 2015. This was followed by a mention of the ocean in a COP decision during COP25 in Madrid, where the Ocean and Climate Change Dialogue was also established.

In 2025, Brazil and France launched a global initiative called the “Blue NDC Challenge,” urging parties to the Paris Agreement to keep in mind the ocean when they update their climate commitments. (READ: 2026 NDC: Philippines promises to reduce more carbon emissions on its own)

“For too long, the ocean has been viewed primarily as a victim of climate change, rather than as a powerful part of the solution,” Lecerf told Rappler in an email. “It has also too often been treated as a separate agenda, when in fact it is central to delivering on countries’ broader climate and development priorities.”
Lecerf said the ocean is integral to energy transition and food security, adding that “the challenge now is to fully recognize and harness this potential.”

blocks.caption: ‘RAHUI.’ Fish swim at a coral reef inside a ‘Rahui’ or restricted area in Teahupo’o, Tahiti, French Polynesia, on August 4, 2024. File photo by Carlos Barria/Reuters

blocks.text: Other organizations holding significant influence in climate and environment discourse are also backing this ocean current at COP31.
“A stable climate depends on a healthy ocean,” the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) said in a paper, released in August, that outlines the organization’s expectations at COP31 for action.

“COP31 should move ocean action from recognition to implementation by establishing it as a core delivery pathway for achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement,” WWF said. This includes, among others, making funding available for countries and communities who need it.
The Philippines is bound by the Philippine Sea, the West Philippine Sea, Celebes Sea, and the Sulu Sea. These waters provide livelihood, home, and transport routes to many Filipinos.
“From the Philippine perspective, the significance of an oceans-focused COP31 is immense,” John Leo Algo, a Filipino climate activist who has been present at many climate summits, told Rappler.
Algo said millions of fisherfolk are at the brunt of the climate crisis, facing the consequences of warmer waters and lower fish catch.
“Food systems and ecosystems alike will be highly exposed to the extreme heat and vulnerable to adverse impacts in at least the next few months,” said Algo.
According to Philippine Environment Undersecretary Analiza Rebuelta-Teh, who is part of the Philippine delegation in Turkey, the Philippines will be supportive of the ocean agenda.
“That is why we have included BMB (Biodiversity Management Bureau) in the delegation to monitor and support the ocean-climate agenda,” Rebuelta-Teh told Rappler in a message.
The Philippines has one of the longest coastlines in the world. It sits at the heart of the Coral Triangle, the global center of marine biodiversity.
In March 2026, the Philippines rolled out a national roadmap that outlined steps to protect and manage the country’s mangrove forests, seagrass beds, and coastal communities.
How this COP31 ocean agenda will translate for communities in the Philippines and other nations remains to be seen. – Rappler.com

This story was produced as part of the COP31 Climate Change Media Partnership, a journalism fellowship organized by Internews’ Earth Journalism Network, Informed Earth, and the Stanley Center for Peace and Security.

articles.title: 19-year-old golfer becomes youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years
articles.summary: Blades Brown became the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years Sunday when the 19-year-old rallied from a seven-shot deficit with a 9-under 63 and beat Ben James with a birdie on the second playoff…

image.caption: Blades Brown of the United States poses with the trophy after winning the World Wide Technology Championship on Sunday in Los Cabos, Mexico. (Getty Images)

blocks.text: Golf·Recap

Blades Brown became the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years Sunday when the 19-year-old rallied from a seven-shot deficit with a 9-under 63 and beat Ben James with a birdie on the second playoff hole in the World Wide Technology Championship in Los Cabos, Mexico.
Birdies 2nd playoff hole to win World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico
Brown became the youngest winner since Charles Kocsis won the Michigan Open in 1931 when he was 18, a tournament that was considered a regional event in the early years of the PGA.

James lost a four-shot lead going into the final round at El Cardonal at Diamante and then showed his moxie by smoking a 285-yard shot into 20 feet on the par-5 18th and making eagle to salvage a 70 and force the playoff.
But he missed an 8-foot putt on the second playoff hole, and Brown made his 3-footer.
"I'm so obsessed with this game. It tests you in so many ways," said Brown, who graduated high school in January. "I love golf, all the stuff that goes into it and I can't wait for what's next."

For a sleepy FedEx Cup Fall event on the southern tip of Baja California, this was pure theater between two players from the next generation. James was the No. 1 player in the PGA Tour University ranking last season. Brown make a surprising choice to turn pro two years ago while a junior in high school.
Brown was tested even more by going through two bags of golf balls on the range waiting to see if the two-shot lead he had over James would hold, and then going back out to the 18th to decide it.

On the first extra hole, their approach shots were side-by-side, separated by about 3 feet, and both narrowly missed eagle chances. They returned to the 18th tee and their drives were next to each other. Both came up just short of the green.

James nearly holed his pitch and saw it run out 8 feet. Brown, who had a similar pitch in regulation that he hit to 6 feet for a closing birdie, this time came up 3 feet short. James' birdie putt grazed the right edge, and Brown poured in the winner.
They have known each since their junior days and Brown figures this is the start.
"I got him this time, but I'm sure we'll be battling it out for years to come," he said.

With eight players separated by two shots on the back nine, Brown ran off three straight birdies to share the lead and then left the mistakes to everyone else. He hit a superb pitch for birdie on the final hole to post at 23-under 265.
That put him one shot ahead of Michael Kim, who played with the Tennessee teen and made birdie from 12 feet for 64 right before Brown made his putt.

Brown earned his PGA Tour card for 2027 by finishing among the top 20 on the Korn Ferry Tour points list. Now he has a two-year exemption, which puts him in the elite Championship Series when the PGA Tour's new model begins in 2028.
The victory also assures Brown of his first major next year at the PGA Championship.
It was another setback for James, who in 13 starts since turning pro has five finishes in the top five, and two runner-up finishes.

Denny McCarthy, winless in nine years in 240 starts on the PGA Tour, made a 30-foot birdie putt on the 13th hole to take the lead. But he hit a pedestrian pitch to the par-5 14th and had to settle for par. With a wedge in hand from the 15th fairway, he came up some 40 feet short and three-putted for a bogey.
McCarthy's tee shot on the 17th was right of the 18th tee box, he put his next shot off a dirt path into a hazard and made double bogey. He shot 69.
Sudarshan Yellamaraju was the top Canadian, finishing tied for 12th at 17 under.
With files from CBC Sports

articles.title: Pope Leo urges Argentina's Milei to put people before the economy
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV has urged Argentina to protect democracy and ensure economic growth benefits the poor, delivering a message to President Javier Milei over austerity, social welfare and political…

image.caption: Despite a rocky relationship with the Vatican, Milei was all smiles on SundayImage: Tiziana Fabi/AFP/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina on Sunday, urging to protect democracy and ensure economic growth benefits the poor.
The pope's remarks were widely watched for criticism of President Javier Milei's harsh austerity programs and cuts affecting social services.
While Leo did not address the government's policies directly, he said "the economy must be at the service of the people, rather than people being at the service of the economy."
Talking to Milei and other government officials, he pointed to the plight of those who, "despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs."
With regards to democracy, he said it was "part of Argentina's heritage that needs to be safeguarded."
The visit to Buenos Aires marks the second leg of the pope's South America tour and is the first papal visit to Argentina in nearly 40 years.

The 71-year old pontiff, who underwent surgery for lung cancer less than a month ago, arrived from Uruguay and is scheduled to visit several cities in the Catholic-majority country before continuing to Peru on Wednesday.

blocks.caption: People were excited about the first papal visit in almost 40 yearsImage: Tomas Cuesta/AFP

blocks.text: Milei's rocky relationship with the Catholic Church
Milei's policies have in the past drawn strong criticism from Argentina's Catholic Church, particularly cuts affecting social services, pensions, disability assistance and public universities.
The Argentine leader, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, has defended his aggressive spending cuts as necessary to stabilize the country's ailing economy and curb inflation.

Annual inflation has fallen from more than 200% to approximately 33% under his administration, but households continue to face financial pressure, and there's been anger over public-sector layoffs and business closures.

In the past, he agressively dismissed criticsm from the Catholic Church, going as far as calling Leo's predecessor, Pope Francis, an "imbecile." He had later though softened his tone and met with Francis in Rome.
On Sunday, Milei struck a significantly more conciliatory note, praising Francis as an "exceptional figure" and the "most important Argentine in history."
Safeguarding democracy
Pope Leo also stressed the need to safeguard democracy in the country.
"Those who exercise authority have a duty to act with prudence, to acknowledge the limits of the power entrusted to them, and to direct their decisions toward the good of the entire community."
The Pope's words carry particular significance ahead of Argentina's presidential election in 2027, in which Milei has said he will seek another term.
The president's aggressive rhetoric and frequent attacks on journalists and political opponents are widely seen as part of an increasing political polarization in the country.
Leo told Milei that strengthening democracy required a "willingness to listen" and the "careful use of words."

His visit marks the first time a pope has traveled to Argentina since John Paul II's trip in 1987. It also brings renewed attention to the legacy of Francis, the country's first pope, who died in April 2025 without returning to his homeland during his 12-year papacy.
Pope Leo starts jam-packed South America tour just weeks after surgery

articles.title: Wagga Wagga family members of alleged DV murderer charged with being accessories after the fact
articles.summary:
Danielle Madgwick died in regional NSW in September after suffering multiple stab wounds to her upper body

  • Get our

blocks.text: Family members of a man accused of the domestic violence murder of a 23-year-old woman in south-western New South Wales have been charged with being accessories to the alleged crime.
Emergency services were called to a Wagga Wagga home on the morning of 19 September where they found Danielle Madgwick suffering multiple stab wounds to her upper body. She died at the scene.

That same evening, Adam Mark Perrim, 31, who was alleged to be Madgwick’s partner, was arrested and charged with alleged domestic violence murder. He briefly appeared in court but did not apply for bail and was remanded to reappear on 18 November.

On Monday, NSW police said they had raided on the weekend the same house where Madgwick was found. Officers arrested two men, aged 18 and 56, and a 53-year-old woman in connection with the alleged murder in mid-September.

blocks.caption: Three people were arrested in Wagga Wagga on the weekend. Photograph: NSW police

blocks.text: The trio was taken to Wagga Wagga police station, with each individual charged with being an accessory after the fact to murder. They appeared in court on Saturday for a committal hearing and were refused bail to next appear on 23 December.
Court documents state those arrested on the weekend were Perrim’s brother, Bailey Perrim, his father, George Maxwell Richard Perrim, and his mother, Julie Ann Collins.
Police will allege in court all three knew Madgwick.
Her death was one of three separate cases across the state investigated as domestic violence-related homicides that weekend.
The New South Wales premier, Chris Minns, said at the time the alleged crimes were “shocking” and his thoughts were with the families and communities of the three women.
Madgwick’s father, Heath Madgwick, paid tribute to his daughter on social media last month on what would have been her 24th birthday.

“Words cannot describe the amount of emotions, thoughts and feelings that have been experienced over the last 4 weeks,” he wrote.

“There’s been enough tears to fill the world’s oceans over and over, I miss you like you wouldn’t believe, your beautiful smile, your silly laugh, our goofy video calls, the groan and eye roll I’d get with every ‘dad joke’, those are memories I’ll treasure for a lifetime.”
According to the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare, a woman was killed every 11 days in 2024-25 by her intimate partner.

articles.title: Trump says he was ‘only kidding’ about making UFC’s Dana White next press secretary
articles.summary:
President says it was ‘just a little fun’ to picture White, UFC boss and Trump’s friend, in briefing room with fighters

Donald…

blocks.text: Donald Trump said on Sunday that he “was only kidding” when he announced a day earlier that he had offered the job of White House press secretary to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC).

Speaking to reporters on his way back the White House from his beach club in Florida, Trump explained the premise of his joke, that if the UFC boss, who is a devoted fan of the president, took over the briefing room, flanked by six fighters, reporters “wouldn’t mess around with him so much”.

“So I was kidding, but I think Dana likes the idea, and he is a very capable guy,” Trump added. “Of course, I was kidding. And you could see that because I put all of the great fighters as his assistants, that they’re all going to come with him … It was just a little fun.”

Earlier on Sunday, the president shared an animated AI cartoon made by one of his supporters on social media, which showed UFC fighters beating up journalists and one, Josh Hokit, repeating the racist remark about Michelle Obama he made during the UFC event at the White House on Trump’s birthday in June.

The president said that his mock announcement that White would become his spokesperson, in a social media post on Saturday, “was an example of something where I was kidding, and then people said, ‘You know, that’s actually a pretty good idea’”.
He did not say who, exactly, supported the idea.

The first in a series of taxpayer-funded pro-Trump ads broadcast by the White House in the run-up to the recent midterms closed with images of the UFC fight on Trump’s birthday and remarks about him from White, who could be heard saying: “He is the toughest, most resilient human being I have ever met in my life.” White used that formulation to describe Trump multiple times during the 2024 presidential election campaign, most notably to sing Trump’s praises at the Republican national convention.

The role of White House press secretary has been vacant for three weeks, since Trump’s previous pick, the far-right commentator Katie Zacharia, was forced to resign after trying, and failing, to dodge questions about why she described herself as an attorney despite having failed the bar exam.

articles.title: SPECIAL COVERAGE: Impeachment trial of Sara Duterte
articles.summary: Rappler brings live updates, analysis, and commentary from reporters and experts as the historic impeachment trial unfolds

blocks.text: LIVE

blocks.caption: SPECIAL COVERAGE: Impeachment trial of Sara Duterte

blocks.text: Rappler brings live updates, analysis, and commentary from reporters and experts as the historic impeachment trial unfolds

MANILA, Philippines – The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte began on Monday, July 6. All eyes are on the Senate which has been convened as an impeachment court, with senators sitting as trial judges.
Rappler’s special coverage brings updates, analysis, and commentary from a panel of reporters and experts, hosted by Rappler columnist John Nery.
Rappler multimedia reporters Jairo Bolledo, Dwight de Leon, and Sundy Locus are at the Senate, bringing you eyewitness coverage of the historic trial.

articles.title: Sara Duterte trial: Defense begins presentation of evidence
articles.summary: The impeachment trial was paused to give way for the Senate committee hearings on the proposed 2027 budget

blocks.text: Defense counsel Atty. Michael Poa makes a manifestation during Day 35 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on October 7, 2026.
Senate Social Media Unit
The impeachment trial was paused to give way for the Senate committee hearings on the proposed 2027 budget

items: Vice President Sara Duterte's defense team will begin presenting evidence in her impeachment trial on November 9 after a suspension for Senate budget hearings.

The defense plans to call corporate, local government, and banking officials as witnesses, including Gencorp's corporate counsel, who will testify about Duterte's alleged business interests but cannot attend the November 9 trial due to a scheduled MRI.
Only one impeachment article regarding unexplained wealth remains against Duterte after three other charges were withdrawn, and the defense will focus on presenting evidence related to this article.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte is set to begin presenting its evidence in her impeachment trial on Monday, November 9, following a weeks-long suspension of proceedings to give way to Senate committee hearings on the proposed 2027 national budget.

A manifestation dated November 4 showed that the defense intends to present corporate, local government, and banking officials as witnesses, including the corporate counsel of Gencorp Industries Incorporated and Metro City Chow Foods — two companies linked to Duterte.

The defense asked the Senate impeachment court to issue subpoenas duces tecum and ad testificandum to Gencorp corporate counsel Suzette Balucanag-Punay, directing her to appear before the court and bring certified true copies and original copies of the companies’ general information sheets, audited financial statements from 2022 to 2025, and other related corporate records covering the same period.

Balucanag-Punay was expected to testify on relevant corporate and business matters, including Duterte’s alleged business interests in Gencorp and Metro City Chow Foods, but she will not be able to attend Monday’s trial due to a scheduled magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan.

“The anticipated date for her presentation will be on Wednesday because the issued subpoena I believe is from Monday to Wednesday. But with the excuse of having this scheduled MRI, definitely, she won’t be able to attend the proceedings on Monday,” House lead prosecutor Representative Gerville Luistro told Super Radyo dzBB.
The defense also sought subpoenas for three Davao City government employees, a barangay chairperson, and at least 16 bank officials.
“We’ve served the subpoena to the 21 witnesses,” Senate Secretary Renato Bantug Jr. said.

The defense earlier asked the impeachment court to subpoena former law school dean Ralph Sarmiento as its first witness. Sarmiento declined, saying he wanted to “preserve the independence of his constitutional law scholarship and the impartiality of his legal views.”

Article 2, which concerns allegations of unexplained wealth against Duterte, is the only remaining impeachment article against the Vice President after the House prosecution panel withdrew the three other articles. With the dropping of charges, the defense will present its evidence on Article 2.
It can be recalled that the impeachment trial was suspended on October 13 to give way to Senate committee hearings on the proposed 2027 national budget. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Maya Jama steps down as Love Island host after nine seasons
articles.summary:
‘Time to throw myself into something new,’ 32-year-old presenter announces on social media while hailing her ‘unforgettable time’ on the show

Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as…

blocks.text: Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of Love Island after three years.
The 32-year-old presenter of the reality TV show made the announcement on Instagram.
Posting a highlights reel of herself on the programme, Jama said it was “time to throw myself into something new”.

“While my own Love Island journey has come to an end, I wish the show and the team all the success in the world, I’ll be cheering you lot on from the sidelines forever,” the TV and radio presenter said.

The move comes after Jama’s stint on the BBC’s Celebrity Traitors, as a traitor who breezed through the series undetected until the finale. Her popularity led to speculation in the Times that she could “get £1m per deal” thanks to her success.
Jama took over from Laura Whitmore as the host when the show returned for its ninth series early in 2023.
She was initially touted as a potential host after it was confirmed Caroline Flack would be stepping down as host in 2019, but the role was given to Whitmore.
Thanking fans and the production team on Love Island, she said she had an “unforgettable time” on the programme.
“I started hosting the show aged 28 and during the nine incredible series met the most wonderful humans along the way. I’ve loved every slow-mo walk, fire pit and live show.”
But she added: “I’ve always believed that to truly grow, you have to take a leap every now and then.”

An ITV spokesperson said: “Maya has been a fantastic and much-loved host on Love Island – we thank her for everything she has brought to the show over the last three years and wish her every continued success.”

Jama moved to London when she was aged 16 to pursue a career in the entertainment industry. She began her broadcasting work co-hosting Trending Live on 4Music and Cannonball on ITV, before moving to present her BBC Radio 1 show on Fridays and Saturdays.
At 23, she became the youngest person to co-host the Mobo awards on Channel 5 in 2017, alongside the JLS star turned presenter Marvin Humes.

items: Following their US midterm election victory, Democrats plan aggressive oversight and investigations into Elon Musk, Stephen Miller, and large companies.
House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries supports impeaching US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, citing his role in unpopular policies.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

WASHINGTON, USA – Tech megabillionaire Elon Musk and President Donald Trump’s newly appointed White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller, and some large companies will likely be targets of congressional probes when Democrats take control of Congress in January, senior lawmakers said on Sunday, November 8.

In television appearances, US Representative Robert Garcia of California and US Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, set to lead the House oversight and Senate banking committees, vowed aggressive oversight after their party’s sweeping midterm election victory.
Meanwhile, House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries indicated he and his fellow Democrats would back an impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Garcia, who is the ranking Democrat on the House oversight committee, said investigations will focus on Musk’s involvement in the Department of Government Efficiency’s firing of federal workers last year, and Miller’s role in Trump’s hardline immigration crackdown.
“I think there’s a lot of interest, not just from our committee, but from committees across the Congress to speak to Mr. Musk,” Garcia told CNN’s State of the Union.
Warren said some companies should be ready for congressional investigations. She did not name any of the companies.
“If you’ve been making your profits by cheating American families and scamming your investors, you’d better get ready for some investigations, serious ones,” Warren told CBS’ Face the Nation program.
Miller — whom Garcia called the architect of a “horrific, unjust” immigration policy — has been promoted to White House chief of staff.
“Stephen Miller is at the center of the major policy decisions that are happening in the administration, and so it does deserve oversight and investigation,” Garcia told CNN.

Voters delivered a historic rebuke to Republicans in the midterm election last Tuesday, November 3, but with Miller as White House chief of staff, the Trump administration is expected to ‌continue its aggressive approach to immigration enforcement, amplify cultural conflicts, and give no ground to a Democratic-controlled Congress, say officials and experts who spoke to Reuters.

The crackdown on immigration, which included operations in which two people were fatally shot in Minnesota by federal agents, has proven widely unpopular. A Reuters/Ipsos poll in October found that only 37% approved of Trump’s handling of immigration, down from 50% when he took office.
Jeffries, who will become speaker of the US House in January, said on Sunday that Democrats would support a measure to impeach Hegseth, a congressional process that could remove him from office.

Representative Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican and Trump critic who leaves Congress in January after a Trump-backed primary defeat this year, has said he will reintroduce articles of impeachment against Hegseth soon. Jeffries said he is a “hard yes” on backing that measure.
“Pete Hegseth has got to go,” Jeffries told ABC’s This Week, citing the defense secretary’s oversight of the unpopular Iran war launched by Trump in February, which has led to a spike in gas prices.
“I believe there will be incredibly strong support for that resolution,” Jeffries added.

Attorney General Todd Blanche signaled on Sunday that the Trump administration was prepared to battle the Democrats in Congress, calling threats by some Democrats to target administration officials and allies “not something we can tolerate in this country.”

“If that’s what this new incoming leadership wants to do, we are ready,” said Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Trump. “If you work in this administration, you have a lawyer. It’s me.” – Rappler.com

articles.summary:
Former police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Paddington in early 20224

  • Get our

blocks.text: Beau Lamarre-Condon has demonstrated in court how he claims he shot Jesse Baird, acting out his movements in the witness box in Sydney.
The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
Giving evidence under cross-examination on Monday, Lamarre-Condon re-iterated his claim that Baird was holding a knife while struggling with the officer in the house.
Lamarre-Condon told the New South Wales supreme court that the knife was next to his throat, which led him to push Baird back with his right arm.
The crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield asked Lamarre-Condon to stand up and demonstrate, telling the accused: “Put your rosary beads down while you do that.”
The officer reenacted the struggle for the jury, with Hatfield describing his movements.

“[The accused] with his left arm out at shoulder height, demonstrated pushing Jesse Baird’s right hand with the knife away from him, so that the left arm was fully extended,” the prosecutor told the jury.

“[Lamarre-Condon] gestured pulling the pistol around the area around his belt … then held it up at around chest or shoulder height and demonstrated with a bent elbow firing a shot towards the right shoulder of Jesse Baird.”
Lamarre-Condon told the court he “discharged a shot” and said he was aiming towards Baird’s right shoulder.
“My arm did extend … I don’t know to what extent … there was constant movement in this struggle,” the accused told the court. “That’s as clear as I can be. This happened very, very quick.”
Hatfield said the officer last week said he was pinned by Baird during the struggle and asked if Lamarre-Condon was now suggesting “something different” by claiming he was constantly moving.

Lamarre-Condon said he was pinned directly before he pushed back and fired the shot, telling the court there was “constant movement” before that.
Asked what Baird and Davies were wearing, Lamarre-Condon said both men were only in their underwear and were not wearing shoes.
During his evidence-in-chief last week, Lamarre-Condon stood by his decision to fire the first shot but claimed a second bullet was “accidentally” fired.
On Monday, he re-iterated he did not intend to fire the second shot at Baird.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Huang admits affair amid rumors of China spy ties
articles.summary: Following reports of Nvidia's chief Jensen Huang becoming involved with a Chinese spy, Huang offered an apology for cheating on his wife. Meanwhile, the US tech company pledged to investigate the…

image.caption: Jensen insisted he was committed to 'supporting America's national security'Image: Lisi Niesner/REUTERS

blocks.text: US tech giant Nvidia said on Sunday it would investigate claims that its CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by "foreign intelligence efforts."

Multiple media outlets, including The Financial Times, recently reported on American intelligence sharing information on Huang's extramarital affair with a Chinese woman. The woman, according to US intelligence sources, had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security.
Chipmaker NVIDIA profits up, despite trade war challenges

The reports identified her as Alice Huang, an executive for Singapore-based company Megaspeed. The US is investigating the company over suspicions that it was helping Beijing bypass export restrictions and obtain cutting-edge AI chips. According to The New York Times, the company has bought Nvidia chips worth billions of dollars in the last two years.
US lawmakers have invited the Nvidia chief to brief them on the reports.
Nvidia's Huang as rich as Warren Buffet
On Sunday, Nvidia's top executive admitted to being "unfaithful" to his wife of 40 years.
"My actions hurt her and our children," Jensen Huang wrote in an email sent to Nvidia staff. "There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."
Nvidia's AI PC explained: AI agents, speed and data privacy
He also said he was he committed to protecting the company and "supporting America's national security."

Huang was born in Taipei and spent part of his childhood in Taiwan before moving to the US. In 1993, he and two other people launched Nvidia, a company that grew to become a leading manufacturer of computer graphic cards and then an essential supplier of computer chips in the AI boom.
Nvidia’s Cage for AI: can it prevent disaster?

The 63-year-old Nvidia CEO is one of the richest people in the world, according to the Forbes magazine, with his $162.2 billion (€145.5 billion) net worth as of Sunday putting him roughly on par with globally renowned investor Warren Buffet.
Huang stays on as Nvidia CEO
In their statement, Nvidia's board of directors said Huang will remain the head of the US-based company while the probe is taking place.
Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," according to their statement.
The board said a group of "independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation."
At the same time, the heads of the $4.5 trillion company said they had "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."

articles.title: North Vancouver soldier who died in Wainwright fire remembered as fearless at funeral
articles.summary: A 23-year-old soldier from North Vancouver was remembered Sunday as a globe-trotting, sporty and car-loving man with an infectious sense of humour and a fearless love for life. A photo of Pte. Aidan…

image.caption: Sonia Monk, Pte. Aidan Goulding's mother, says one of the hardest parts of losing someone so young is losing the opportunity to build on her relationship with him. (CBC)

blocks.text: A 23-year-old Canadian soldier was remembered Sunday as a globe-trotting, sporty and car-loving man with an infectious sense of humour and a fearless love for life.

Hundreds of military personnel, family and friends gathered at an armoury on a stormy day in Vancouver to remember Pte. Aidan Goulding, one of four soldiers killed last month after a grass fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta overtook troops during a training exercise.
His mother, Sonia Monk, described her son as someone with a great sense of humour, always open to a good laugh.
"Whenever I was disciplining him, he would start to laugh or he would try to say something. I could never properly discipline him," she said.
"That's something that our family is going to miss. Nothing is going replace that."
Sonia Monk says Goulding and his fellow soldiers who died in the CFB Wainwright fire "will not be forgotten." (CBC)
Monk said she was proud of her patriotic son who joined the army from a high-paying job.
"When he finally told me, he said, 'I have one life to live, I want to do something important, and so I'm joining the army.' I think that's so unselfish of him," she said.
After he joined the Canadian Armed Forces, Goulding felt like he found a place where he belonged, Monk said.
"It gave him a sense of purpose, a family and a place he truly felt at home."
Goulding's funeral started with soldiers carrying his flag-draped casket into the armoury, with the sounds of a bagpipe cascading, and some words from a rabbi.
Monk described his upbringing in North Vancouver with his brother, Wylder, who was also his best friend.
"They had each other's backs," she said. "Their relationship touched my heart deeply, and I was content in knowing that they would always be close."

items: Funeral mourners recall friendship, dedication of sergeant killed in CFB Wainwright incident
Mother of soldier killed at CFB Wainwright says he wanted to protect Canada

blocks.text: Growing up, he showed his competitive and curious side.
His family said in a statement he played many sports, including soccer and rugby, and developed a love for cars at a young age.
He spent many hours buying used cars, fixing them late into the night under the glow of a lamp on his family's driveway and then reselling them.
The first car he fine-tuned was a used Chrysler 300C.
The modification: make it louder.
"He loved understanding how things worked and took great pride in making them his own," his family said.
He was also stylish.
Monk said her son asked to wear a white suit on his first day of Grade 4. When he turned 21, he asked for a gold suit.
"He was unapologetically himself, and I admired that," she said,
The family has also described Goulding as a globe-trotter.
Sonia Monk, Pte. Aidan Goulding's mother, says joining the Canadian Armed Forces gave Goulding "a sense of purpose." (CBC)
In his short life, he explored many parts of the world, including Mexico, Germany, Austria, Italy, Croatia, Malta, the Netherlands, England and Spain.
Reagan Goulding, his aunt, said during the funeral that he often made those around him laugh.
She said it's been hard knowing that he died at a young age.
"This is perhaps one of the hardest parts of losing someone so young," she said. "It's not just the memories we have lost, but the opportunity to make a relationship we still had time to build."
Reagan Goulding said she could see her nephew, who she described as being "smart, ambitious, determined, and resourceful," perhaps becoming a police officer or joining CSIS.
"I truly believe great things were in his future. We wanted him to know that we all saw this in him, that we believed in him and became a proud follower of him," she said.
She said her last message to Goulding was sent on the day of the tragedy, a text message that said, "Aidan, you better be OK."
She never received a reply.
Who are the 4 service members killed at CFB Wainwright?
Reagan Goulding said if she knew this was her last message she would have said more, including telling him one more time how proud she was.
She also remembered the other soldiers killed in the fire.
They were: Pte. Hayden Lykkemark, 19, of Langley, B.C.; Sgt. Morgan Wong, 26, of Edmonton; and Pte. Shaun Farrell, 23, of Prince Albert, Sask.

"They were young men who matched their calling, who stood beside one another, and who were parts of the family themselves. Their loss is felt by their families, their friends, soldiers, and everyone who has been touched by this tragedy," she said.
"Aidan and his fellow soldiers will not be forgotten," she added.
As the soldiers carried the casket out of the armoury and reloaded it into a hearse to head to the cemetery, the sun broke through the clouds, casting its light over rainy Vancouver.
Monk, who spoke to media after the funeral, said she felt it was a sign from Goulding, encouraging her to move forward with life.

"Because I think through tragedy or hardship, he would always say things like that, 'We'll move forward.' So, I think that's what he was sort of saying to me today, actually, with the sun shining bright in my eyes."
Monk said she felt "supported and lifted" after hearing stories from Goulding's "brothers and sisters" in the army.

"I'm quite tired, I haven't eaten a lot, I haven't slept a lot. But all the support and seeing everybody here today, it's remarkable. I can't find a word other than remarkable," said Monk, adding that "There's lots of love in Canada."

articles.title: LIVE UPDATES: Sara Duterte Impeachment Trial (November 9, 2026)
articles.summary: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte resumes on Monday, November 9, 2026, with the defense team set to present its witnesses. Here are the latest news and updates.

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte will resume Monday after nearly a month-long suspension, with the defense set to begin presenting its case-in-chief.

The defense team has listed over 20 intended witnesses for November 9 to 13, with law professor Dean Ralph Sarmiento being the first. He, however, declined to testify as a witness and the defense later withdrew its request to the impeachment court to subpoena him.

Given that Sarmiento will no longer be presented as a witness, the defense is expected to push through with Atty. Suzette Balucanag-Punay, the corporate counsel of Gencorp Industries, Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corporation—two of the entities linked to the Vice President.

Balucanag-Punay is set to testify on relevant corporate and business matters linked to Duterte and produce certified true copies and/or original copies of the General Information Sheets, Audited Financial Statements, and all other related corporate records from 2022 to 2025.

But House lead prosecutor and Batangas Representative Gerville Luistro earlier said the defense could also resort to “dilatory tactics" when the trial resumes, such as filing a demurrer to evidence or insisting on presenting evidence related to the three Articles of Impeachment that the prosecution had withdrawn.
She said Duterte’s counsel might attempt to raise matters concerning the dropped articles during the proceedings, but the prosecution would oppose such moves.

“Bagaman prerogative nila 'yan to file the proper remedy they believe will be appropriate given the situation, we're really hoping na mag-proceed sila sa presentation of evidence,” Luistro said last week.
(Although it is their prerogative to seek the appropriate remedy they believe is warranted under the circumstances, we are really hoping they will proceed with the presentation of evidence.)

During the trial on October 13, the House prosecution panel dropped three out of the four Articles of Impeachment leveled against the Vice President, saying its case would stand on Article II alone on alleged unexplained wealth due to non-full declaration of assets and non-divestment of business.

The withdrawn impeachment articles were: Article I on confidential funds; Article III on bribery; and Article IV on assassination plot, grave threats, and inciting to sedition against President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former Speaker and incumbent Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez.
The impeachment court will convene at 10 a.m. today and will suspend trial in the afternoon to pave the way for the plenary session. —Giselle Ombay/LDF/KG, GMA News

articles.title: GPs to offer 300,000 patients extra support to ease winter strain on NHS
articles.summary:
£40m scheme in England aims to keep most vulnerable people well at home and avoid unnecessary hospital stays

Hundreds of thousands of vulnerable patients in England are to receive extra…

blocks.text: Hundreds of thousands of vulnerable patients in England are to receive extra support from their GP as part of a £40m drive aimed at keeping them out of hospital this winter.

As the NHS gears up for the pressures of the coming months, family doctors will offer 300,000 people with frailty and long-term conditions health checks, medication reviews and respiratory tests designed to prevent avoidable hospital admissions.

Funded by cash reallocated from existing GP budgets for 2026-27, the scheme will allow surgeries to identify and provide extra care to the patients they believe are most at risk of becoming seriously unwell in the winter. Groups of GP practices can use £126 for every eligible patient supported.
The prime minister said the scheme would be targeted at patients with heart disease, frailty and lung conditions such as emphysema and other types of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
Andy Burnham said he was “not going to pretend this winter will be easy” but the programme would help keep people well at home and avoid unnecessary trips to hospital.

“If we want to take the pressure off our hospitals this winter, we’ve got to keep people well at home. So we’re backing GPs to reach the most vulnerable people early, before a small problem turns into a trip to A&E,” he said.

“People deserve the right care in the right place. And our NHS staff, who work so hard, deserve the right tools to provide it. I’m not going to pretend this winter will be easy. But with new technology, upgrades for hospitals and more care available closer to home, we’ll make sure the NHS is there for everyone when they need it.”
The health secretary, Yvette Cooper, said the scheme had been designed to offer greater support to the frailest patients.

“After such a heavy summer for our NHS as a result of the heat, everyone is working together to prepare for more challenging winter pressures,” she said. “That includes the rollout of flu vaccinations, investing in extra urgent care capacity and strengthening partnerships with social care.

“With thousands more GPs in post and millions more GP appointments this year, the £40m programme to support vulnerable patients in the community is part of our plan to help patients, improve primary care and also to support our NHS through the heavier winter months.”

Prof Victoria Tzortziou Brown, the president of the Royal College of GPs, said she welcomed the focus on prevention and supporting patients at greatest risk of avoidable hospital admission this winter.
“GPs’ clinical expertise, knowledge of their patients and continuity of care are central to identifying those most in need and providing personalised, coordinated support,” she said.

But she also said short-term initiatives alone could not deliver “sustained improvements in care” that patients with complex health needs required. Instead, she said, a longer-term approach to prevention was necessary, which must be backed by “sustainable investment in general practice”.

Two doctors were eating near the city's Main Market Square on Saturday when a gunman began firing at random, killing six and injuring 15.
"We rushed into the area and started our rescue" before the emergency services arrived, Pędziwiatr said.
The pair raced to treat both the attacker and two officers shot while subduing the perpetrator.

articles.title: Man charged with murder over fatal stabbing of HungryPanda delivery rider in Melbourne
articles.summary:
Footscray man charged over death of 47-year-old Feng Jianming in the CBD on Friday night

  • Get our breaking news…

blocks.text: A man has been charged with murder after a delivery rider was stabbed to death while working, leaving his family bereft and a city in mourning.
On Friday night, HungryPanda delivery rider Feng Jianming, 47, and another rider confronted a man allegedly tampering with their bikes in Melbourne’s city centre.
An altercation ensued and the man, a 51-year-old, is alleged to have stabbed both riders.
Emergency services rushed to the scene on Frederick Way, but Feng could not be saved.
The second rider, 34, was taken to hospital with serious injuries, where he remained on Monday.
The 51-year-old was arrested by police on Saturday and on Monday morning was charged with one count of murder and intentionally causing serious injury.
Feng, originally from China’s Shaanxi Province, had been in Australia for about nine years.
His wife, Xu, their four parents and two children all relied on his hard work to get by at home.
The news of Feng’s death reverberated through Melbourne and gig worker communities in Australia and abroad.
Mourners left floral tributes and notes near the state library over the weekend in his memory.
Some cards expressed sympathy for his family, while others vented grave frustrations with messages such as “city of criminal” and “Asian lives matter”.
A GoFundMe fundraiser set up by the Melbourne Chinatown Business Association had raised almost $390,000 by Monday morning to help Feng’s family with emergency travel and funeral expenses.
Food delivery company HungryPanda said it was assisting the family with visa arrangements, funeral expenses, financial support and insurance.
The 51-year-old man was remanded in custody to appear before Melbourne magistrates court on Monday.

articles.title: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes
articles.summary: Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows damage to the building in the capital's central financial district.

blocks.text: The Aramco Tower, a skyscraper in the Saudi Arabian capital's central financial district, had been hit by an air attack.
A statement issued via the Houthi-controlled Saba news agency confirmed the group had targeted Riyadh's business zone on Saturday, without mentioning the Aramco Tower by name.
The Saudi energy ministry said the tower had suffered only "minor damage" and no one had been killed or injured.
Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows more extensive damage to the building, with at least one floor appearing to have been badly hit by a missile or drone strike.
Windows on more than one level appear to have been shattered by the strike.
The Houthis also said Riyadh's airport and Aramco oil storage facilities were targeted in separate strikes. Saudi Arabia said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed several missiles.
The strikes were the latest claimed by the Yemen-based armed group against targets deep inside Saudi Arabia, which the Gulf power has struggled to contain in recent months.
It came a day after the Houthis accused a Saudi-led coalition of killing at least 33 people, including women and children, in an air strike on Yemen.
Footage broadcast by Houthi-run television channel Al Masirah showed rescuers pulling bodies from the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.
Saba said 39 people had been injured in the strike. Saudi Arabia has not commented.

A Saudi-led coalition has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government, which has lost control of a large swathe of the country to the rebel group.
Although the conflict had largely been dormant in recent years, fighting has intensified following the outbreak of the Iran war.

An informal ceasefire unravelled in July after the Tehran-backed Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they have called a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport Saudi Arabia said had been to prevent an Iranian aircraft from landing there.
Major fighting has since resumed between Houthi forces and troops aligned with Yemen's Saudi-backed government.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.

articles.title: ‘Seismic shift’: Native American women made significant gains in US midterms
articles.summary:
Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary candidates in Tuesday’s elections, report says

The US midterm elections saw voters

blocks.text: The US midterm elections saw voters elect a slew of historic representatives – from the country’s first Muslim senator to the first Black female governor – but among the most significant gains were those for Native American women.

On Tuesday, voters elected the first Native American woman governor, senator and leaders of two tribal nations. Nationwide, voters elected at least 75 Native women or non-binary and Two Spirit candidates in the November midterms, according to Advance Native Political Leadership and the news site ICT.

Deb Haaland, a citizen of Laguna Pueblo and Joe Biden’s former interior secretary, will lead the state of New Mexico. Peggy Flanagan, a member of the White Earth band of Ojibwe and current Minnesota lt governor, will represent her state in the US Senate. Crystalyne Curley will become the first woman to lead the Navajo Nation, one of the country’s largest tribes. And Tina Abrams will lead the Seneca Nation of Indians in western New York, also the first woman leader in the modern history of the state’s largest tribe.
Mary Peltola, who is Yup’ik, could join Flanagan as another first Native woman in the US Senate pending the results of her still undecided race in Alaska.

“This is a seismic shift that is happening in our communities,” Jordan James Harvill, a citizen of the Cherokee Nation and strategist with Advance Native Political Leadership, told the Associated Press.

Although Native Americans have made significant gains in political power in recent years, it has been a long road to get here. Native Americans have only been allowed to vote across the entire United States since the 1960s. In 1985, Wilma Mankiller became the first woman elected to serve as principal chief of the Cherokee Nation.

In 2018, Haaland and Sharice Davids, a member of the Ho-Chunk Nation, became the first women elected to Congress when they both won seats in the House of Representatives alongside a wave of progressive freshmen lawmakers, including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Ilhan Omar and Rashida Tlaib. Davids was easily re-elected last week in Kansas to a fifth term in Congress.

“The first thing that made [running for office] feel really possible was seeing Deb Haaland, was seeing Sharice Davids on a national level,” New Mexico state senator Angel Charley, who is Laguna/Zuni/Diné, told the Guardian about her decision to enter state politics in 2024.

In 2020, after an outpouring of voters from the Navajo and Hopi reservations in Arizona saw the long-red state vote for Biden, he named Haaland to lead the interior department, making her the first Indigenous cabinet secretary.
The same year, Yvette Herrell, who is Cherokee, became the first Republican Native woman elected to Congress. She served from 2021 to 2023.

This election cycle, a record-setting 363 Indigenous candidates ran for office in local, state and federal elections across the country – with at least 180 of them winning their races. Among them were Claire Valdez, a citizen of Ysleta del Sur Pueblo and Democrat from New York, who will join Davids in the US House of Representatives.
The Senate has seen four Native men represent their states in its 237 year history, but Flanagan will be the first Native woman to join the chamber in January.
At her victory party in St Paul, Minnesota, Flanagan told supporters: “I could not run for the US Senate without Native women. I could not exist in the way that I do without Native women.”
For Haaland, the historic nature of the election isn’t lost on her – but in the final weeks of a hectic campaign she told the Guardian that she sometimes forgets she’s on the verge of a milestone.

“Sometimes I forget about the fact that I would be the first Native woman. We’re in the throes of this statewide campaign and it’s so busy and we’re trying to be everywhere all at once,” she said in a recent interview. “But I recognize that for some people who feel like they haven’t ever been represented – I really, I’m grateful that I have this opportunity … I just hope that I can help folks to see that hard work still means something. That anyone can be a leader regardless of where you come from or how much money you do or don’t have.”
In 2023, New Mexico became the first and only state in the country to implement an updated Native American Voting Rights Act, which gave tribes greater input on polling locations and redistricting.

For the Navajo Nation, the largest tribal nation by geography – spanning approximately 27,000 sq miles across parts of New Mexico, Arizona and Utah – Curley’s victory in tribal elections also held on Tuesday was significant. Curley is currently the speaker of the Navajo Nation council and became the first woman to hold that position in 2022.

“As women, we have to work twice or triple as hard, especially within Navajo politics,” she told the AP, adding that she faced sexist rhetoric during her campaign. “This is a win for all Navajo women.”

“I am humbled,” Abrams, the Seneca Nation’s president-elect said in a statement after her victory. “Tonight, at long last, a woman will now lead our Nation as president. This is a moment inspired by generations of strong Seneca women who came before me, and one that I hope inspires generations of Seneca women who come after me.”

articles.title: Iran: Trump says strikes unlikely if peace talks keep moving
articles.summary: After weeks of rumors that the US and Israel were preparing new strikes on Iran, President Donald Trump said it was "highly unlikely" that he would order a new escalation as the Iranians "want to…

image.caption: Trump has hinted at new Iran strikes during the recent election campaignImage: Umit Bektas/REUTERS

blocks.text: In an interview with US broadcaster CNN, President Donald Trump sought to downplay fears that the US is about to relaunch its military campaign against Iran.
"It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," he told CNN on Sunday. "The answer is highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."
At the same time, Trump restated that the US military was "ready" to launch a new round of strikes and could "finish [Iran] off."
"I've got three aircraft carriers here," he said. "They're fully locked and loaded."
He added that the US military had 38 bridges in their sights "that we can knock down in literally one hour."
US strikes Iran hours before midterm election
However, Trump also repeated several times that the new escalation is "highly unlikely," saying that Iran was a "failing nation" and "withering away financially" after eight months of hostilities.
"I hit them so hard. You don't know how hard I hit them," he said. "They want to make a deal so badly."
Iran and the US stuck between war and peace

Trump ordered an attack on Iran in late February, after US ally Israel launched what it called a "preemptive strike" on its biggest regional rival. The US president has since repeatedly declared victory, insinuated that Iran was begging the US for a deal, and told the media that a peace deal was done or nearly done.

Iran has repeatedly rejected Trump's account. Despite Trump's claims that Iran was collapsing both economically and militarily, Tehran has been able to repeatedly stage attacks on US allies in the region and maintains at least a partial blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The Houthi rebels in Yemen, allied with Tehran, are currently targeting high-profile targets in the Saudi capital of Riyadh and elsewhere across Saudi Arabia.

The most tangible diplomatic achievement since the start of the war was reported in June, when Iran and the US signed a memorandum of understanding in Islamabad. But the talks broke down and the memorandum expired in August, with the two sides still engaged in a military and diplomatic stalemate.
Iranian top diplomat says US still digesting midterms
The conflict has proven to be unpopular with the US public, featuring heavily in the campaign for US midterm election that eventually saw Trump's Republicans lose their majorities in Congress.
Republicans rebuke Trump on Iran war, economy after midterm wipeout
On Sunday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that that peace mediators did not "travel" since the Tuesday election in the US. Araghchi described the outcome as a "shock."
"We now have to see how long it will take for them to digest these results, in order to determine how we are going to move forward," he said.
Qatar says talks moving behind the scenes

Qatar, which acts as one of the mediators in the conflict, denied rumors that the US and Iran are failing to reach a peace deal. On Saturday, the Qatari prime minister said both sides were still working toward an agreement.
Separately, the Reuters news agency cited a senior Iranian official as saying that Tehran has submitted a proposal on its nuclear program to Washington through Qatar.
The official also noted that further talks would depend on the US meeting Tehran's demands, including the lifting of sanctions, unfreezing Iranian funds and war reparations.

articles.title: Cruise ship pianist rescued after nine hours treading water miles from shore
articles.summary: Man taken to hospital after falling off Royal Caribbean ship in Pacific Ocean, with Coast Guard investigating incident A pianist for a Royal Caribbean cruise ship is expected to survive after two…

blocks.text: A pianist for a Royal Caribbean cruise ship is expected to survive after two Newport Beach, California, fishermen discovered him treading water in the Pacific Ocean nearly 20 miles (32km) offshore on Friday.
The unidentified man was taken to the hospital after the rescue, according to the US Coast Guard, which is now investigating how he went overboard from the cruise ship.

Authorities believe the man may have been in the ocean for approximately nine hours before he was spotted by Sean Norton and Grant Garrett, who were returning from a fishing trip near Catalina Island.
The two fishermen had spent the morning fishing for marlin when their trip took an unexpected turn. By noon, they had pulled the stranded man from the water.
“I’m like, ‘Yeah, it’s a human being. Stop the boat; let’s get all of our lines in,” Garrett told CBS News, recalling the moment the boat’s captain first saw the man in the water.

The fishermen quickly worked together to bring the man onboard. Once the man regained his composure, Garrett said he identified himself as a pianist onboard Royal Caribbean’s 14-deck cruise ship, the “Ovation of the Seas.”
According to Norton, the rescued crew member had few words to describe what he had just experienced. “The only thing he said to me was, ‘Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,’” Norton said.

After the rescue, the fishing crew issued an emergency maritime call, prompting Newport Beach lifeguards to respond and provide assistance. Battalion chief Adam Yacenda said the man was found approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, according to CBS, or “pretty much in the middle of the ocean”.
Despite the extended time spent in the water, Norton believes unusually warm ocean temperatures may have played a significant role in the man’s survival.
“You have this crazy super El Niño year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water’s 76 degrees,” Norton said. “A different year, no way he makes it.”

The circumstances surrounding the crew member’s fall from the cruise ship remain under investigation by the Coast Guard. Royal Caribbean Group acknowledged the incident and said it is assisting the employee following the ordeal.

In a statement to CBS, a company spokesperson said: “We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share.”

articles.title: Norway says it has been bumped by the IIHF to allow Russia to compete at world juniors in Canada
articles.summary: The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said Sunday it has been informed that it is being bumped by Russia from competing in the world junior championships in Canada, a decision creating further…

image.caption: Norwegian team reacts after a 2026 IIHF Ice Hockey Men's World Championship semi-final match in Zurich. The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said Sunday it has been informed that it is being bumped by Russia from competing in the world junior championships in Canada. (Fabrice Coffrini/ AFP via Getty

blocks.text: Hockey

The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association said Sunday it has been informed that it is being bumped by Russia from competing in the world junior championships in Canada, a decision creating further uncertainty involving the 10-nation tournament.
The world juniors are set to open in Alberta on Dec. 26

The switch, the NIHA said, comes in the wake of the Court of Arbitration for Sport's recent ruling reinstating Russian hockey teams to compete internationally, beginning with the world juniors set to open in Alberta on Dec. 26.

There remain complications in the decision, which has yet to be formally announced by the International Ice Hockey Federation. The IIHF's website still includes Norway as a participant in a tournament featuring the top men's players under age 20.
Russia, however, is not guaranteed of competing after Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he will bar the team from entering Canada, leaving open the possibility of Norway still being included.

"The situation is still unclear," Norway's ice hockey secretary general Peter Salsten said in a statement posted on the association's website and translated from Norwegian to English. "This makes us hope that the last word has not been said about our participation in Canada."

Other complicating factors involve six nations, including Norway, vowing to boycott games against Russia as long as the war in Ukraine is ongoing. Several long-time corporate sponsors also have said they will drop out if Russia competes.

Norway acknowledged that the IIHF has been handcuffed by the court's ruling. As the 10th-ranked team entering the tournament, Norway said it was relegated to the 1A Division to open the spot for Russia.

blocks.text: The Russians haven't competed in the tournament since a fourth-place finish in 2021, with their ban beginning after the nation invaded Ukraine in February 2022.

"We are aware of the status and the measures the IIHF feels compelled to take, and will await further information from the IIHF in the coming days," Salsten said. "This also clearly shows all the practical challenges and immediate consequences for everyone involved when countries are reinstated immediately."

articles.title: Germany: Chancellor Merz to nominate Aigner for president
articles.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced that he will nominate Ilse Aigner for federal president, paving the way for her to be the first woman to hold the office. DW has more.
articles.byline: Jon Shelton, Saim Dušan Inayatullah, Timothy Jones

image.caption: Merz (left) and Aigner have known each other since 1998 [FILE: October 2026] Image: Alexandra Beier/AFP

blocks.text: Published November 8, 2026last updated November 8, 2026
Merz to nominate Aigner as Germany's next federal president

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced to the Christian Democrat Union (CDU) party heads his intention to nominate Ilse Aigner as the country's next federal president, according to the dpa, AFP and Reuters news agencies.
She will replace Frank-Walter Steinmeier when he steps down at the end of his term early next year.

Aigner, who hails from Bavaria's conservative Christian Social Union (CSU) and is the president of the Bavarian state parliament, would be the first woman to hold the German president's position should she be elected on January 30.
Steinmeier is a member of the junior coalition partner SPD.
Merz will officially pitch Aigner's name for the job on Monday, when party leaders will gather to choose a joint candidate.
SPD and Green Party representatives have already voiced support for her candidacy.

articles.title: Small plane crashes into pickup truck on busy Florida highway
articles.summary: No one was injured after emergency landing in Fort Myers 50 minutes after takeoff with two people onboard A small plane crashed into the rear of a pickup truck as it made an emergency landing on a…

blocks.text: A small plane crashed into the rear of a pickup truck as it made an emergency landing on a busy Florida highway on Saturday but miraculously no one was injured in the dramatic incident.
Video footage obtained from the sheriff’s office shows a Cessna 172 grazing over the truck as it approached the ground for a complete landing on a road in Fort Meyers at about 11.45am on Saturday.
The aircraft made an emergency landing after the pilot reported an engine issue, according to a Federal Aviation Agency (FAA) statement.
The plane took off from Sebring, Florida, around 11am on Saturday before it made the emergency landing about 50 minutes later, according to flight tracking data.
There were two people on board the aircraft and the pickup truck was traveling eastbound on Bayshore Road.
There were no reported injuries on the scene, according the Lee county sheriff’s office.
“Couldn’t have been a better outcome. Grateful doesn’t come close!” Carmine Marceno, Lee county’s sheriff, shared in a post to X.
LCSO Patrol & Florida’s department of transportation safely relocated the aircraft while the FAA is working to assume the investigation, Marceno added.
The FAA is the lead agency on the investigation into the incident.
The emergency landing comes one week after a business jet carrying nine people nose-dived into a south Florida neighborhood and erupted into a giant fireball.

articles.title: Weather challenges search for Vancouver Island man who failed to return from canoe trip
articles.summary: A search is ongoing after James "Dakota" Smith, 34, failed to return from a solo canoe trip off northern Vancouver Island amid stormy weather Friday. Authorities were called to search for Smith after…

image.caption: Relatives say James "Dakota" Smith was last seen around 12 p.m. PCT Friday, Nov. 6, 2026. (Ma'amtagila Tribe Society/Facebook)

blocks.text: British Columbia·New

A search is ongoing after James "Dakota" Smith, 34, failed to return from a solo canoe trip off northern Vancouver Island amid stormy weather Friday. Authorities were called to search for Smith after he was a few hours late to return home to his partner and two young children.
Canoe found 6 nautical miles away from where James 'Dakota' Smith was reportedly last seen
A community-led search is underway off northern Vancouver Island for 34-year-old James "Dakota" Smith, who failed to return from a solo canoe trip amid stormy weather Friday.

Smith, a member of the Ma’amtagila Nation, was last seen around 12 p.m. PCT at Adam River, about 85 kilometres northwest of Campbell River, according to family member and search co-ordinator Matthew Ambers.
Smith had planned to return bones from an earlier hunt to nature by dropping them into the ocean, according to his cousin Seneca Ambers.
Returning bones to nature, Seneca said, is a traditional practice among Ma’amtagila First Nations people.
"We just want him home," she said.
Authorities were called to search for Smith after he was a few hours late to return home to his partner and two young children, Seneca said.
According to Matthew’s post, search and rescue crews located Smith’s canoe about seven-and-a-half hours after the search began — six nautical miles west of Adam River.
His posts also called on the community to assist with the search.
"As soon as the sun came up [Saturday], [Matthew] wanted to make sure that people were out searching for Dakota," said Seneca.
Community search
She said most of those searching Saturday were family and community members, including "a lot of friends" who drove to the Adam River area from various locations across Vancouver Island.
Seneca said Smith and his family are considered "guardians of our territory" and he is experienced in the wilderness.
James "Dakota" Smith is a member of the Ma'amtaglia Nation. (Ma'amtagila Tribe Society/Facebook)
"We don’t know what’s happened," she said.
In a post to on social media, shortly after Smith was last seen, the province issued a high streamflow advisory for parts of B.C., including eastern Vancouver Island.
That stormy weather continued to challenge search efforts Saturday, Seneca said, as rough conditions on the water forced Matthew to retreat from the water and aid in the land search instead.
"We want to think as positive as possible right now. That he’s just found a place to hunker down," she said. "But obviously there’s a lot of fear and worry."

blocks.text: In an email, Victoria’s Joint Rescue Coordination Centre said it received the call on Nov. 6, and two Canadian Coast Guard vessels and two aircraft were tasked with searching for Smith.
The canoe was recovered, however there were no signs of Smith.
The centre said that based on survivability models, a search reduction was ordered at roughly 7:30 p.m. PCT.
"The RCMP has the lead now," read the email.
The RCMP says it received the report about Smith at approximately 4:20 p.m. PCT, as the search continued in the Johnstone Strait.

articles.title: Many killed after migrant boat sinks off Senegal
articles.summary: The incident occurred near Kebemer off the coast of northwestern Senegal. Authorities on El Hierro in the Canary Islands have declared an emergency after a marked increase in migrant boat arrivals.

image.caption: Thousands of people attempt to reach Spain's Canary Islands from West Africa through the perilous Atlantic route every yearImage: Jesus Cabrera/REUTERS

blocks.text: At least 34 people were killed after a small boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of northwestern Senegal, according to the Senegalese Press Agency.
Thousands have died in recent years after embarking on boats from the Senegalese coast in order to reach Spain's Canary Islands through the perilous Atlantic route.
Initially, the Senegalese Ministry of the Interior stated that only one person had been rescued from the capsizing and that 21 bodies had been recovered.
The ministry added that the toll was "provisional" and that search operations were still ongoing.
The incident occurred near Kebemer, some 180 kilometers (around 112 miles) north of the capital, Dakar.
On Saturday, the ministry stressed the government's "determination to combat people smuggling networks, notably through strengthened cooperation with neighboring countries."
Senegalese authorities said they intercepted 142 migrants on a similar boat aimed at reaching Spanish territory on Friday. The boat included nationals of multiple West African countries.

blocks.caption: Authorities on the island of El Hierro have declared an emergency due to increased migrant arrivalsImage: Jesus Cabrera/REUTERS

blocks.text: El Hierro island declares emergency over migrant arrivals
Authorities on El Hierro Island in the Canary Islands declared an emergency on Saturday after a marked increase in migrant boat arrivals.
El Hierro officials say that over 3,300 people have arrived on around 30 boats since the start of the month.
"We are very concerned... by this sharp increase in arrivals," Alpidio Armas, head of the El Hierro regional council, told Spanish television.
"This is precisely what has led us to declare an emergency in order to ensure a framework of cooperation with higher-level institutions," he added.
Armas said that conditions at the island's hospital have become "undesirable."
El Hierro is home to about 11,400 residents.
Migrant arrivals reached a record high of 46,000 in 2024. Afterwards, arrivals have fallen sharply due to increased surveillance and cooperation with African countries.
